evaluationApproach.summary: The AI must evaluate Nutritionist candidates on evidence-informed sports nutrition, youth safeguarding, practical fueling, hydration, interdisciplinary collaboration, ethical boundaries and clear communication. Licensing and permitted scope vary by jurisdiction; never infer clinical authority from the title alone.
evaluationApproach.corePrinciple: Strong answers provide age-appropriate, feasible, evidence-informed nutrition support while respecting professional scope, confidentiality, consent and referral responsibilities.

mandatoryRules.rule: Score against Nutritionist responsibilities, not Head Coach, physician, clinical dietitian or performance coach duties.
For questions requesting a real situation or example, do not award 4/4 unless the response includes the situation, the candidate's action and the outcome.
Distinguish generic healthy-eating advice from soccer-specific, safe, practical and individualized support.
Treat relevant but generic responses as Acceptable or Good, not automatically Strong.
Flag material written/video contradictions for human review, not automatic rejection.
Do not infer registration, clinical privileges, prescribing authority, anti-doping competence or verified outcomes.
Evaluate job-relevant content, not accent, appearance, age, gender, ethnicity, disability or video quality.
Do not reward unsupported clinical claims, restrictive plans, jargon or response length.

calibrationOverall.strongestAreas: Youth welfare, fueling basics, hydration, professional boundaries and collaboration
calibrationOverall.mainWeaknesses: Outcome measurement, individualized follow-up, formal planning and evidence of results
calibrationOverall.summary: The fictional candidate demonstrates a sound general approach to soccer fueling, youth welfare, communication and professional boundaries. Responses appropriately emphasize collaboration with qualified clinicians and safeguarding. However, evidence of program outcomes, formal monitoring, individualized follow-up and first-90-day milestones remains limited. A recruiter should verify qualifications and request examples of player education plans, travel protocols and measurable follow-up.

questions.text: What qualifications, experience and scope of practice prepare you to support soccer players?
strong: Identifies training, applicable registration or licensure and relevant age groups.
Explains supervised experience and referral boundaries.
Provides a concrete example of soccer-related work.
questions.acceptable: Describes relevant background but limited role-specific examples.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Claims medical or clinical authority without appropriate credentials.

calibration.response: I studied nutrition and supported an academy wellness program for two seasons; clinical issues were referred to a registered dietitian.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Shows relevant practical and ethical judgment, but stronger outcome evidence, verified experience or detailed procedures would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: How do you define the nutritionist's role within a soccer club or academy?

questions.acceptable: Recognizes education and collaboration but not clear decision rights.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Promises diagnosis or treatment outside permitted scope.

calibration.response: I help players understand everyday fueling and communicate general plans with coaches and medical staff.

questions.acceptable: Asks about food and training but omits important context.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Prescribes restrictive diets without assessment or appropriate oversight.

calibration.assessment: Shows relevant practical and ethical judgment, but stronger outcome evidence, verified experience or detailed procedures would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: How do you adapt fueling guidance to training intensity, position and match schedules?

questions.weakOrConcerning: Uses a single rigid meal plan for all players.

calibration.response: I suggest more substantial fueling around double-session days and work with staff to understand weekly demands.
